---
title: "Research"
---

Our group investigates how ice sheets, glaciers and snow interact with the
atmosphere and ocean, on timescales from decades to glacial cycles. This work
depends on numerical models that are fast enough to simulate many thousands of
years or to run large ensembles, while still representing the relevant
physical processes. For this reason, a large part of our effort goes into
developing such models and making them openly available.

## Model development

::: {.tool-card}
### Yelmo ice-sheet model

Yelmo is a thermomechanical ice-sheet model that can be applied to any ice
sheet, from present-day Greenland and Antarctica to the ice sheets of past
glacial periods. It solves for ice flow with a choice of approximations to the
Stokes equations (e.g., the shallow-ice, shallow-shelf and depth-integrated
viscosity approximations). We use Yelmo to study ice-sheet tipping points,
paleo ice-sheet evolution and long-term sea-level rise. Yelmo runs as a
stand-alone model or coupled to CLIMBER-X, and a Julia version (Yelmo.jl) is
under development.

Robinson, A., Alvarez-Solas, J., Montoya, M., Goelzer, H., Greve, R., and Ritz, C.: Description and validation of the ice-sheet model Yelmo (version 1.0), *Geosci. Model Dev.*, 13, 2805–2823, [doi.org/10.5194/gmd-13-2805-2020](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-13-2805-2020), 2020.

[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> fesmc/yelmo](https://github.com/fesmc/yelmo){.repo-link}
:::

::: {.tool-card}
### CLIMBER-X Earth system model

CLIMBER-X is a fast Earth system model (fESM) that couples a
statistical-dynamical atmosphere to a three-dimensional ocean, sea ice, a land
surface with dynamic vegetation and an interactive carbon cycle. It simulates
on the order of 10,000 years per day, which makes it suitable for glacial
cycles and for large ensembles of future projections. We use CLIMBER-X to
study the stability of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC),
variability in the Southern Ocean and the long-term response of the ice sheets
to warming.

Willeit, M., Ganopolski, A., Robinson, A., and Edwards, N. R.: The Earth system model CLIMBER-X v1.0 – Part 1: Climate model description and validation, *Geosci. Model Dev.*, 15, 5905–5948, [doi.org/10.5194/gmd-15-5905-2022](https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-15-5905-2022), 2022.

[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> cxesmc/climber-x](https://github.com/cxesmc/climber-x){.repo-link}
:::

## Fast Earth system modeling community

Yelmo and CLIMBER-X are part of a wider effort to develop fESMs as open,
modular software. The [Fast Earth System Modeling
Community](https://github.com/fesmc) hosts Yelmo together with related
components, such as the snowpack model
[Chion.jl](https://github.com/fesmc/Chion.jl), models of glacial isostatic
adjustment and basal hydrology, and tools for preparing input data. CLIMBER-X
is maintained by the [CLIMBER-X Earth System Modelling
Community](https://github.com/cxesmc). Each component can be run stand-alone or
coupled within a fESM, which allows individual processes to be tested before
they are used in long coupled simulations.

## Collaborations

Our model development is a long-standing collaboration with the following
partners:

- **Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM):** Marisa Montoya and the
  [PalMA ice-sheet modeling group](https://www.palma-ucm.es/palma-ice).
- **Instituto de Geociencias (IGEO, CSIC-UCM):** Jorge Alvarez-Solas.
- **Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK):** Matteo Willeit and
  Georg Feulner.
